levels.headline: Anthropic asks to sell its shares to the public on the Nasdaq
levels.body:
Anthropic is a company that builds artificial intelligence, including an assistant called Claude. It has now made public its plan to sell shares in the company on the Nasdaq stock exchange. This is called an initial public offering, or IPO. The company would use the ticker "ANT". It had told the US regulator about its plans in private in June.
The papers say seven founders will have 50.1% of the votes on company matters. This means they can keep control. A group called the Long-Term Benefit Trust, which picks most of the company's board, also stays.
Reports say the papers warn about the risks of AI and say that two customers brought in almost a quarter of 2025 revenue. A date for the sale has not been given.
levels.why: If it goes ahead, ordinary investors could buy a piece of a leading AI company.

levels.headline: An AI company has asked to sell its shares to the public
levels.body:
Anthropic is a company that makes artificial intelligence, or AI. One of its products is called Claude. This week it made public its plan to sell shares to the public. A share is a small piece of a company. The first time a company does this, it is called an IPO. The company would use the short name "ANT" on a stock market called the Nasdaq.
Seven founders will keep 50.1% of the votes about company matters. So they will stay in control. A special group called the Long-Term Benefit Trust also stays. It chooses most of the company's board.
Reports say the papers talk a lot about AI risks. They also say that two customers brought in nearly a quarter of the money in 2025. No sale date has been set.
levels.why: Share sales like this can make companies bigger, and let more people own a piece of them.

levels.headline: A company that makes AI has said it wants to sell its shares
levels.body:
Anthropic is a company that builds AI, which is computer software that can write and answer questions. One product is called Claude. This week Anthropic told the world that it wants to sell shares to the public. A share is a tiny piece of a company. When a company sells shares for the first time, it is called an IPO.
Seven of the people who started the company will keep 50.1% of the votes about how it is run. So they keep control. A group called the Long-Term Benefit Trust also stays. It picks most of the company's board.
The papers also warn about the risks of AI. No date for the share sale has been set yet.
levels.why: It could let more people own a small piece of a big technology company.

levels.headline: An AI company says it wants to sell shares to the public
levels.body:
Anthropic is a company that makes AI. AI is computer software that can write, answer questions and help people. One of its products is called Claude. This week, Anthropic said it wants to sell shares in the company to the public. A share is a tiny piece of a company. The first time a firm does this, it is called an IPO.
The people who started the company will keep over half of the votes on how it is run. This means they stay in charge. A special group also helps pick the company's board.
The papers say a lot about the risks of AI. They also say that two customers bring in a lot of the company's money. There is no date yet.
levels.why: People will be watching to see how much the company is worth.

levels.headline: An AI company wants to let people buy a piece of it
levels.body:
Anthropic is a company that makes AI. AI is a computer helper that can write and answer questions. This week, Anthropic said it wants to let the public buy tiny pieces of it. These tiny pieces are called shares. When a company first does this, it is called an IPO.
The people who started the company want to keep over half of the votes. That way, they can stay in charge of big choices.
The papers the company shared also talk about the risks of AI. They say that AI could be dangerous if it is not looked after well.
Nobody knows yet when the sale will happen.
levels.why: Many grown-ups will watch to see if AI companies are a good place to put money.

levels.headline: A company that makes computer helpers wants to share a little of itself
levels.body:
Imagine you have a big cake. You decide to sell small slices to people who want to buy them. You still keep a big piece, so you decide what happens to the rest. That is a bit like what a company called Anthropic wants to do.
Anthropic makes a clever computer helper called Claude. Now it wants to sell tiny slices of the company, called shares, to the public. The people who started it want to keep over half the votes, so they can stay in charge.
The company has also written down that computer helpers could be risky if they are not looked after well.
Nobody knows yet when the sale will happen.
levels.why: It lets more people join in, and it shows how big clever computers have become.
